title: A Chiral 60-Metal Sodalite Cage Featuring 24 Vertex-Sharing [Er4(μ3-OH)4] Cubanes

synthesis.procedure: L-Threonine and NaBr were added to aqueous Er(ClO4)3. The mixture was stirred at about 80 °C while freshly prepared aqueous NaOH was added slowly until incipient, persistent precipitation at pH 6. It was filtered hot; the covered supernatant was left on a gradually cooling heating plate. Crystals were filtered and dried under dynamic vacuum at room temperature for 24 h.

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide
reagents.amount: 1.0 M aqueous solution; volume not reported

synthesis.temperature: about 80 °C during addition; gradually cooled for crystallization; room temperature during drying
synthesis.time: crystals appeared after 2 days; dried for 24 h
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered hot; supernatant covered with Parafilm and gradually cooled; pink crystals filtered and dried under dynamic vacuum.

properties.summary: The decreasing χMT on cooling was attributed chiefly to thermal depopulation of crystal-field-split Er(III) states; the authors describe the cluster as magnetically isolated.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Sixty Er atoms form a sodalite-like cage assembled from 24 vertex-sharing Er4(μ3-OH)4 cubanes. Its eight hexagonal faces contain templating carbonate ions; the core can also be described as an outer 24-Er shell surrounding an inner 36-Er shell.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the procedure for 1, replacing L-threonine with D-threonine: ligand and NaBr were added to aqueous Er(ClO4)3, followed by slow addition of aqueous NaOH at about 80 °C to pH 6. The hot mixture was filtered, gradually cooled to crystallize, and the crystals were filtered and vacuum-dried.
